proposals.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich, wide-gap aluminosilicate. Its high Li content should also suppress Li-consuming reactions with Li6PS5Cl, and it adds an untested Al-containing silicate family.
proposals.motivation: Li3PO4 was the best coating so far (penalty about 0.19 eV/atom, bin 9), but every tested coating still reacted with Li6PS5Cl to release S/SCl species. Li-rich oxides with no or weakly bound polyanions (Li2O, Li8SiO6) and the Li-rich borate Li3BO3 did not improve on that, so a Li-rich Al/Si framework is the next untested direction.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 5 eV), electronically insulating oxide that is chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte. Its phosphate anion is hard to oxidize at 4.0 V and it does not readily reduce against Li6PS5Cl. It is a well-known protective coating for cathode interfaces, so it is a strong first candidate under the insulation and band-gap criteria.

LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating fluoride with high oxidative stability at 4.0 V vs Li. Its fluoride anion is hard to oxidize, and LiF is a thermodynamically stable Li salt that is generally unreactive toward sulfide electrolytes. Compared with Li3PO4, which reacted with Li6PS5Cl to release SO2 and SCl4-type products (penalty 0.34 eV/atom), LiF may give a lower contact-reaction penalty. It is also a chemically different family, so it tests whether the halide coating reduces the interfacial penalty.

Its chloride is also less prone to oxidation than the fluoride-driven pathway at 4.0 V, so it is a chemically distinct test of a halide coating that is compatible with the sulfide.
